summary.text: An 89-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, coronary artery disease, status after CABG and hysterectomy presented with a left forearm mass that developed during several months. She had no lymphadenopathy and no B-symptoms.

The excised 3 × 2.2 × 2 cm skin mass showed a dense intradermal lymphoid population, diffuse in the upper dermis and nodular or follicular deeper, with scattered Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg like cells. Immunostains, FISH for IgH-bcl2 fusion, and PCR for immunoglobulin heavy chain, T-cell receptor and EBV DNA were reported, with the fusion, rearrangements and EBV markers negative.

The authors reported the case as primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma with Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg like cells. Given the localized disease, no other treatment was initiated, and the patient was lost to follow-up.
